Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full software with (all) file(s), in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code. Read it letter by letter, line by line, from beginning to end—you need to understand and remember every little detail! Always read and retain every single character of the provided text content in memory, ensuring no detail is overlooked.

entries.answer:
Below is a single, comprehensive prompt that rewrites the provided specification as an implementation brief for building the full system from scratch. It preserves the technical intent of the source, including the requirement for complete production-ready code, a single-file delivery model, exhaustive component coverage, real interactivity, strict token architecture, and no placeholders or simulated content. The source describes a browser-based IDE and software creation platform implemented as a fully inlined single-page application with client-side routing, extensive design tokens, layered CSS architecture, pane management, editor, terminal, file tree, agent chat, canvas, deployment, billing, account, modal, animation, and workspace subsystems.[1]

```text
Build a complete, production-ready, browser-based integrated development environment and software creation platform as a single-page web application delivered entirely in one file named index.html. The entire application must be implemented from scratch with all HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fully inlined inside that single file. Do not use external stylesheets, external scripts, placeholder markup, mock content, dummy states, fake actions, simplified demos, incomplete scaffolding, or simulated subsystems. The only permitted external references are the explicitly defined font file paths. Every screen, control, component, interaction, state transition, route, layout region, panel, overlay, and workflow described in the technical specification must be fully implemented in complete, unabridged, production-ready code. All views must be reachable through client-side routing within this one file. Never mention or reference any preexisting product, codebase, or original software by name.

Start by defining the full document shell. The html element must use lang="en", class="replit-ui-theme-root notranslate", translate="no", and inline style "-webkit-user-select: none;". The head must include UTF-8 charset, responsive viewport meta, the exact favicon path, the exact keywords meta content, and a single style block containing every font declaration and all CSS. The body must include class mapping to the default typography treatment and exactly one root mount element for the application. A single script block must contain the entire application logic, including routing, rendering, state management, event handling, layout coordination, pointer interactions, keyboard interactions, virtualization, drag and resize logic, pane orchestration, menus, overlays, drawers, editor integrations, terminal emulation, and all subsystem behavior.

Define all required @font-face rules first, outside any CSS layer. Include all required font families, variable ranges, styles, italic variants, mono variants, branding variants, pixel variants, masking fonts, compatibility variants, and their exact source paths. Preserve the specified font-display behavior, supported weights, italics, feature settings, and compatibility loading behavior with @supports where required.

After font declarations, declare CSS layers in this exact order at the top of the style block: @layer reset, base, rui-wind-properties, components. Implement the reset layer by applying box-sizing to all elements and pseudo-elements, resetting margin, padding, and border globally, defining the responsive column-count layout variables, and setting html line-height to 1. Implement the base layer by styling body, form controls, and interactive primitives, applying the default font family, foreground color, and root background color, removing default button appearance, and enforcing the required touch-action behavior for pressable elements. Implement the rui-wind-properties layer by declaring the required border-style and outline-style custom properties on all elements and ::backdrop using the specified cross-browser support pattern. Put all component-specific rules in the components layer.

Define the complete token system on :root exactly as specified. Include the full spacing scale, border radii, shadows, typography families, font sizes, line heights, font weights, border width, breakpoints, and transition tokens. Then define the full light-theme token set on the root theme class, including all background, foreground, outline, accent, brand, interactive, surface, and text variables. Add the full dark-theme overrides inside prefers-color-scheme: dark. All color, spacing, and typography variables must inherit correctly and support contextual overrides through surfaces and themed regions.

Build the utility class system within the specified layer. Implement all required background, opacity, text color, text alignment, typography size, font family, font weight, border, display, flexbox, overflow, positioning, sizing, gap, padding, margin, radius, cursor, selection, truncation, and transition utilities exactly as described. Generate the spacing-based utility variants programmatically or manually, but include the full required coverage.

Construct the full application layout as a fixed full-viewport shell with a top workspace header, a main content region, a collapsible task sidebar, a central workspace content region, and a mobile footer. Use CSS custom properties for header height and sidebar widths. The main workspace must support a pane system with absolute positioning, perspective-based transforms, z-index control, box-shadow, dimensions, transitions, border radii, and padding variables. Each pane must include a pane header and pane content region. Implement at least four fully functional pane types: code editor, terminal, agent chat, and preview. Support drag-resizing on all edges and corners with correct cursors, hover expansion behavior, pointer events, and touch support.

Implement the drawer system with both the mobile bottom sheet variant and the side sheet variant. Include transform-based open and close behavior, backdrops, drag handles, height constraints, retreating and advancing states, and backdrop opacity variables. Implement the mobile tab pager as a horizontal snap-scrolling interface with a sticky animated header band. Apply the specified z-index hierarchy consistently across workspace content, panes, floating chat, modals, popovers, lock screen, analytics inspector, and cookie-consent-level overlays.

Implement all navigation systems: dock, nav menu, breadcrumb items, avatar dropdown, and inbox button. Match the required spacing, dimensions, radii, active indicators, dropdown widths, section divisions, selected states, overflow behavior, and notification dot positioning. Every interactive element must be keyboard accessible, visually styled, and operational.

Implement a full code editor pane using CodeMirror 6 with the exact theme structure and all requested editor styling details. Apply the specified background, content typography, gutters, selection colors, cursor styling, placeholder appearance, fold placeholder styling, search match styling, tooltip styling, autocomplete panel styling, syntax token color mappings, font sizes, active line gutter styling, search panel styling, goto-line panel styling, lint panel styling, URL underline treatment with favicon rendering, multiplayer tooltip behavior, completion info layout, hover tooltip delay animation, contextual AI tooltip styling, vim panel input styling, placeholder layer behavior, readonly caret behavior, snippet editor behavior, ghostwriter hint appearance, signature suggestion layout, LSP documentation formatting, search results styling, diff and patch viewers, and editor wrapper structure. All described editor panels, tooltips, autocomplete states, diagnostics behavior, and animations must exist and function.

Implement a full terminal pane using xterm.js-equivalent behavior and DOM structure. Recreate the required root terminal styling, hidden helper textarea, composition view, viewport, rows layer, cursor layer, selection layer, link layer, decorations, overview ruler, custom scrollbar, sticky terminal layout wrapper, and shell execution styling. The terminal must be interactive and visually integrated into the pane system.

Implement a virtualized file tree driven by CSS variables and absolute row positioning. Each row must use the required row height, indentation, icon sizing, padding, scroll container behavior, footer, drag preview behavior, and drop preview system. Only render visible rows. Support expanding and collapsing directories, status indicators, unsaved markers, drag-and-drop previews, and virtualization based on scroll position.

Implement the full AI chat subsystem with both embedded and floating behavior. The floating variant must respect the specified bottom-left placement, max width, and max height behavior. Create the chat feed, turn rows, session separators, composer, tool blocks, shell execution cards, webpage visit cards, web search cards, screenshot blocks, empty session state, loading skeleton, and floatie backdrop. Maintain scroll anchoring behavior exactly as specified so new messages do not cause visual jumpiness. Every row, tool block, and chat control must be real and interactive.

Implement the synced canvas subsystem with the required font override, shape-properties toolbar placement, toolbar separators, scrim cutouts, ghost frame rail, breathing scrim animation, onboarding glow, and planning border overlays. Include all required animations and canvas-adjacent UI elements. The canvas surface and overlays must participate in the same design system and pointer model as the rest of the application.

Implement the deployment UI, including the deploy button, status dot, domain management panels, DNS record accordion, deployment-in-progress view with collapsible logs and embedded terminal, scheduling interface, execution list, quick deploy dialog, and all associated state displays. The deployment subsystem must be functional at the UI level with real data flow and interactive state transitions rather than static cards.

Implement billing and plan management interfaces, including overview cards, field rows, shimmer loaders, usage measure bars, usage limit bars, plan badge interactions, credit slider, and generic slider component with track fill behavior driven by custom properties. Apply the exact dimensions, borders, animation timing, and responsive behavior.

Implement the home dashboard, including recent projects, project cards, application cards, grids, hero sections, responsive search, fade-in behavior, star-hover controls, footer treatments, and responsive layout changes across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints.

Implement user profile, account settings, avatar system, organization switchers, and authentication pages. Include sticky sidebars, account settings layout, avatar badges, font treatments, branded auth typography, rebrand upsell region, and prompt pill animation. All layouts must follow the token system and adapt correctly at desktop and mobile widths.

Implement all modal and overlay systems, including underlays, centered dialogs, fullscreen dialogs, side dialogs, popup dialogs, popovers with placement-sensitive animation origins, lock screen overlays, publish popovers, and import overlays. Respect the specified z-index values, pointer-event behaviors, transition timing, dimensions, inset handling, and responsive adjustments.

Implement all loading states and animation systems, including shimmer loaders, three-rectangle loaders, animated ellipsis, status dots, workspace-header icon pulse, tour shimmer, tour glow, tour pulse, fade-ins, and all other named animations in the specification. Wrap motion behavior in reduced-motion-safe media queries or provide reduced-motion overrides for every animation.

Implement missions view, organization management tables, invite dialogs, multiplayer manager lists, settings side sheets, workspace header, task list scrollbars and masks, section toggle buttons, workspace right header, workspace loading state, workspace content containers, design subagent card animations, floatie card stack behavior, and every other subsystem described in the source specification. Do not omit later sections because they appear after long component descriptions. The implementation must cover all described sections end to end.

Use virtualization wherever the specification requires it. File tree rows, project grids, agent feed items, layers, history lists, and any other large collections must render only visible DOM nodes and position them absolutely using row height and index calculations. Never render large off-screen node sets when virtualization is required.

Implement complete pointer, drag, touch, and keyboard support. All drag handles, resize handles, canvas overlays, and pane interactions must use touch-action: none and support both mouse and touch pointer events. Manage focus visibility globally by setting data-focus-visible on the html element on Tab or Shift+Tab keydown and removing it on mousedown. Ensure keyboard navigation, focus rings, semantic structure, and accessible labels are correct throughout. Respect reduced motion preferences globally.

Handle responsive behavior rigorously. Use the specified breakpoints, container queries, column count changes, mobile side sheet behavior, mobile footer behavior, desktop drag regions, mobile auth adjustments, project grid adaptation, home layout changes, and workspace header container-based truncation. Add the required iOS toolbar tint bars to prevent Safari toolbar bleed. Use retina-safe half-pixel borders where specified at high device pixel ratios.

Maintain exact design-system consistency. Use the defined variables for spacing, color, border radii, typography, transitions, backgrounds, surfaces, outlines, accents, and shadows. Preserve theme inheritance, light and dark mode parity, and surface semantics. All borders, shadows, hover states, selected states, overlay opacities, notification dots, pills, cards, headers, footers, buttons, inputs, tooltips, menus, drawers, and panes must derive from this token system rather than ad hoc values except where exact literal values are explicitly required.

Do not simplify the system. Do not collapse multiple components into generic substitutes. Do not replace requested subsystems with static mockups. Do not omit routes, editor panels, overlays, drawers, deployment interfaces, billing interfaces, profile pages, organization management, canvas controls, or workspace utilities. Do not use lorem ipsum, “coming soon,” fake progress, non-functional buttons, or cosmetic-only widgets. Every view must render real UI with actual interactive state and all routes must be reachable.

Deliver the final result as one fully self-contained, production-ready index.html file containing the entire application, with all HTML, CSS, JavaScript, fonts referenced only from the allowed font paths, complete client-side routing, complete component coverage, complete styling coverage, complete state handling, complete interactions, complete responsive behavior, complete accessibility behavior, complete reduced-motion handling, and no missing sections, no placeholders, no stubs, and no references to the original software or codebase.
```

If you want, I can also produce a second-pass version that is even more compressed and optimized specifically for another language model to execute as a build prompt, while preserving the same requirements.[1]
